# Delivery stages and acceptance

## Stage 1 — first implementation commit

Implement COMMIT_01.md: interactive LangGraph loop, typed core API tools, configuration, continuity, persistence, visible operations, bounded spend and a real smoke check. This stage is not the full Idea C demo.

Meaningful checks: tool schema validation; correct source/error envelopes; cumulative budget across turns; permission denial; bounded retry; thread isolation and resume; secret redaction. Mock calls are test fixtures, not live-data proof. An actual model-tool API run is a separately recorded smoke check.

## Stage 2 — full evidence investigation

Add question/claim records, baseline vendor/customer/professional discovery, targeted people and indexed social adapters, origin-aware extraction, identity/timeline matching and customer comparability. Retain comprehensive gathering with adaptive depth. Use saved probe cases for development, then unseen subjects; never hardcode results.

Acceptance: correct vendor/customer, exact evidence for answers, no conversion of repeated marketing into independent confirmation, no direct contract inferred from an intermediary, attributed employee claims, and explicit cannot verify for unsettled facts. Record what additional research changes.

## Stage 3 — decision deliverable and event adapter

Generate concise question answers with expandable evidence dossier, matrices and validation actions. Adapt actual organizer request/response format. Keep factual answer status separate from run completion. Add configured client rules, limits and requirement versions.

## Stage 4 — robustness and event rehearsal

Exercise wrong-entity/namesake, duplicated testimonials, sparse evidence, old customer deployment, recent relevant event, denied/redirected/truncated source, deadline and lower-budget change. Kill/restart around tool dispatch and finalization. Unknown in-flight outcomes must be visible; completed captures are reused according to freshness policy.

Measure full-run elapsed time, model/search/provider costs and retry costs. Provide proposed INR service price separately from measured economics and assumptions. No validated willingness to pay is established.

## Event facts from supplied PDF

Seven-hour build; requirement change at hour 3; organizer repo with commits throughout; README buyer/input/result/pass mark/data sources; architecture showing calls, approvals, retries and ledger; hidden/unseen requests; live real-world data for at least one decision. Cases involve a record/event after 1 September 2026; old context is not forbidden. Approval precedes irreversible external actions, if any. Core public research has none by default.

Finals: 3-minute demo including kill/restart, 5-minute live fix, 2-minute questions and 2-minute changeover. Weights: live run 20, robustness 15, design 15, ethics 25, financial feasibility 25. Open track alone must submit three correct-answer cases by 11:00 AM. Exact organizer formats and client request must be obtained; do not invent them.

Source: [supplied problem statement](C:/Users/goyal/Downloads/ContextCon05_BITS_Problem_Statement.pdf), pages 1–4. These are document requirements, not proof we implemented them or authorization for external actions.
